text: 🇲🇽🚗 "Made in Mexico, for Mexico." "For 11 years, under the firm conviction of 'Made in Mexico for Mexico,' Kia México has grown alongside the Mexican economy." — Young Sam Kim (Andy Kim), CEO of Kia México Kia has been a top-5 brand by volume in Mexico since 2018 and will hit 1 million vehicles sold here by the end of this year. 65% of what it sells in Mexico is already built in Mexico — a share that now grows with the EV3, which will also be exported to Latin America and other markets.

🇲🇽✊ "As a Mexican, I can tell you: we have the best talent in the world." "The learning capacity of the Mexican worker is unmatched anywhere else." — Marianela Calderón, Administration Director, Kia México Kia's Pesquería plant was just certified the #1 auto plant in the Americas for quality, productivity and sustainability — ahead of 70+ plants from every brand on the continent. One in three Kia México employees is a woman; 85,000 people work across its supply chain.

🇲🇽🏠 After 34 years, FOVISSSTE is building social housing again. "Today is a historic day for state workers. After 34 years, FOVISSSTE is building social housing again... The loans are in pesos, with fixed payments. At FOVISSSTE, UMA loans are over." — Jabnely Maldonado, FOVISSSTE Executive Director, at the groundbreaking in Puebla First stone laid for the "Carmen Serdán" complex: 512 homes. National commitment: 100,000 homes for workers earning 1-2 minimum wages, backed by at least 60 billion pesos. Each complex will be named after a woman from Mexican history.

🇲🇽📈 Mexico's investment portfolio reaches $404 billion across 1,186 projects. "As of today, the investment portfolio holds 1,186 projects — in final planning stages or already running — worth $404 billion dollars." — Ximena Escobedo, Undersecretary of Industry and Commerce 13 more projects already hold fast-track authorization through the Presidency's Investment Office. Biggest sectors there: telecom and energy. In the broader portfolio: automotive and manufacturing.

🇲🇽🤝 Mexico buys more from the US than China, Germany and Japan combined. "Mexico is the number one customer of the United States. If you add China, Germany and Japan, we buy more from the US. That's why we've worked to keep this relationship." — Marcelo Ebrard, Economy Secretary, after Trump again downplayed the USMCA Ebrard said Mexico got "the best deal" of any country in last week's tariff decisions — which he said explains why Mexican exports to the US keep growing. Next round of talks: first week of September, Washington DC.

🇲🇽🏭 "We're already working — not just waiting to see what happens." "Experts said there would be no more auto investment in Mexico because of tariffs. What's happening? GM will build here the vehicle it imported from China. And today Kia invests $649 million in a vehicle built only in Korea." — Marcelo Ebrard, Economy Secretary Ebrard also confirmed Toyota is NOT leaving Mexico — it is moving one production line and keeping its Guanajuato plant. "Mexico will keep producing vehicles, and we'll send them to many countries."

🇲🇽⚡ Kia will build its first fully electric vehicle in Mexico — the EV3, starting August 4. "For the first time in our history we will produce and sell a fully electric vehicle in Mexico. The EV3 will be proudly made in Mexico." — Horacio Chávez, Commercial Director, Kia México Kia announced a $649 million investment (2026-2028) to retool its Pesquería, Nuevo León plant — a vehicle built today only in Korea. 500 new jobs this year, 1,500 more by 2030. National content starts near 27%. Buyers get a home charger included; a 10-80% charge takes 30 minutes.

text:
🇲🇽🏭 <u>KIA BETS $649M ON MEXICO'S FIRST EV LINE</u>

Kia will invest $649 million in Mexico between 2026 and 2028 to produce the EV3 — the first fully electric vehicle made in the country — at its Pesquería, Nuevo León plant, with production starting August 4. While Trump claims his tariffs are pulling automakers out of Mexico, one of Asia's biggest carmakers just made its largest bet yet on Mexican manufacturing.

🇲🇽🎒 <u>PROFECO DEPLOYS 55 BACK-TO-SCHOOL FAIRS NATIONWIDE</u>

Mexico's consumer protection agency Profeco is rolling out 55 back-to-school fairs across the country starting July 31, running through September 4: school uniforms, books, backpacks, stationery and shoes at preferential prices, plus free haircuts, medical certificates and birth certificate services. Mexico City's main fair lands at Expo Reforma on August 15-16. Defending the family budget is public policy, not charity.

🇲🇽⚖️ <u>VULCAN LOSES AT ICSID: MEXICO PAYS LESS THAN 1%</u>

US firm Vulcan Materials sued Mexico at ICSID for over $1.7 billion after its Calica quarry in Quintana Roo was shut down over environmental violations. The tribunal threw out nearly every claim: Mexico will pay about $17 million — less than 1% of the demand — tied to a single closure in January 2018, under Peña Nieto. Sheinbaum was clear: the company must now repair the environmental damage in Playa del Carmen, and the land stays a Natural Protected Area. The investor-state arbitration racket blinked.
